title: Micropatch SDK Walkthrough Journal
content:
Daily scratch / playbook: micropatch SDK walkthrough (personal log)

Context
- Goal: quick, reproducible walkthrough for new devs to get the Node + Python SDK sample app running and verify streaming and function-calling examples. Make it 15-20 mins end-to-end. Focus on smallest surface area that still shows production-relevant bits (auth, streaming, error-handling, model selection).
- Current pain points noticed while pairing and during office hours: example versions drift, tokenization note missing, streaming example drops first 1-2 tokens in Node example, python env setup assumes poetry which many folks don't use.

Today's objectives (micro-sprint)
1) Reproduce the streaming token-drop locally and capture minimal repro steps.
2) Sketch a new single-file tutorial for Node that avoids extra dependencies and uses fetch + ReadableStream.
3) Draft a short error-handling sidebar: when to retry vs when to fallback to smaller model.
4) Update README snippet that calls out "pin model version" and how to do a canary route in the Console.

Quick log (times approximate)
- 09:15 — clone fresh: git clone https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk ; checkout main.
- 09:25 — ran node examples/streaming-demo.js; observed first-token drop consistently on my M1 mac. Filmed a 20s clip for QA.
- 09:40 — tried replacing SDK fetch polyfill with native fetch; token-drop persists. Suspicion: middleware in example buffers initial chunk.
- 10:10 — instrumented example to log raw chunks before join; found an empty string chunk emitted first. Likely code path that collects chunks does slice/filter incorrectly.
- 10:25 — small patch idea: change chunk filter from `if (chunk) parts.push(chunk)` to `if (chunk !== undefined)` and ensure initial newline handled. Note: must test with longer sequences and Windows node.
- 10:45 — paired with Aisha over Slack call; she suggested adding an explicit flush in the first chunk handler to avoid dropping.

Notes for docs edits (high priority)
- Node streaming example: replace the streaming helper with minimal ReadableStream consumer example. Include explicit backpressure notes.
- Python tutorial: add alternative setup using venv + pip install -r requirements.txt (quick steps). Many workshop attendees use pipenv/poetry but we should show 1 simple path.
- Authentication note: remind users to set REDWOOD_API_KEY env var; show `export REDWOOD_API_KEY=...` and Windows PowerShell equivalent.
- Model pinning: show `model: "redwood-v1-small@2026-02-15"` example; add one-line about how Console rollouts can map a logical route to multiple model versions. Link to Console rollouts doc.
- Troubleshooting checklist: include tiny items: check region mismatch, token limit errors, mismatched content-type, CORS header headers for browser fetch.

Ideas for sample app (unique angle)
- "Memory microapp": simple Node + SQLite demo that shows streaming chat with prefix caching (KV caching example). Focus: show cost-savings by avoiding repeated encoder ops. Could be used in Optimize talks.
- CLI tool example: single-file script that calls embeddings to do quick local search over README snippets. Low friction for demos.

Open questions / decisions
- Do we keep the existing multi-file example for completeness or retire it in favor of the single-file walkthru? I vote to keep both but surface the single-file first.
- How opinionated should the tutorial be about SDK config? (e.g., recommend batching config defaults). Suggest: document recommended defaults but show how to override.
- Should we include a small section on cost estimation for the sample app? Yes — at least show a simple token->cost calc snippet.

Actionable TO-DOs (next 24h)
- [ ] Create PR with node streaming example rewrite (Tess). Linked draft: https://github.com/redwood-inference/sdk/pull/482 (WIP).
- [ ] Add python venv quickstart to tutorials/README (Tess).
- [ ] Draft troubleshooting sidebar and add to SDK docs page (Aisha).
- [ ] Prototype memory microapp README + minimal code (Luca).
- [ ] Add unit test that runs streaming example in CI against local mock to catch first-chunk empty-string regressions (add ticket DOC-314).

Tiny implementation notes/snippets (scratch)
- Node streaming consumer idea (pseudocode):
  const res = await fetch(url, opts);
  const reader = res.body.getReader();
  while(true) { const {value, done} = await reader.read(); if(done) break; const text = new TextDecoder().decode(value); // push even if text=='' but skip undefined
  }

- Cost calc snippet (js):
  function estCost(tokens, ratePerK = 0.002) { return (tokens/1000)*ratePerK; }

- Quick retry strategy rules (for sidebar):
  * fast 429s: exponential backoff starting at 200ms, max 3 retries
  * 5xx: retry once after 1s then fallback to smaller model route
  * parse errors: do not retry, surface to user + link to troubleshooting

Loose notes for PR description (what to call out)
- Repro steps for token-drop + short test case
- Why change: reduces surprise for browser + node users; avoids dependency bloat in examples
- Backward compat: keep old example in examples/legacy/ and point to it from the new README

Random reminders to self
- File a tiny UX bug about Console rollout UI wording ("promote" vs "rollout").
- Remind docs team to add the model version date format convention to styleguide.

End-of-day status
- Streaming repro captured, small patch sketched. Node tutorial rewrite started (30%). Python quickstart added as a TODO. Meeting with product to clarify rollout wording scheduled tomorrow 11:00.

Attachments / artifacts to include in final PR
- short screen recording (10-20s) showing token drop (I uploaded to slack thread above)
- unit test that simulates empty first chunk (small fixture)
- README updated with one-file Node walkthrough and Windows envvars

If I don't finish: leave clear checklist in the PR and tag Aisha as reviewer.

-- Tess
(leave for morning handoff)
